name: Askja and Víti crater from Dreki
region: Dyngjufjöll, Vatnajökull National Park, north highlands
why: From the Dreki huts over the bare lava and tephra of Dyngjufjöll into the Askja caldera, to the milky Víti crater on the shore of the great Öskjuvatn lake.
book: Highland F-roads only (F88, F910, F894), open roughly July to September: a 4x4 or the summer bus/tour from Mývatn. Sleep at the Dreki huts of Ferðafélag Akureyrar (book ahead) and ask the rangers there about the route. From Víti a 2.5 km path leads north to the Vikraborgir car park, where the bus and tours stop.
water: Fill up at Dreki: there is no drinkable water on the way.
dangers: The path down into Víti is slippery, and rock and mud slides happen: keep to the rim if in doubt.
Snow patches into July, and sudden fog and cold on the plateau at 1,100-1,350 m.
Do not leave the marked path: the ground near the lakes can be closed after landslides.
turnaround: Fog on the plateau or the rangers advise against it: take the road to Vikraborgir instead.

points.name: Drekagil huts
points.note: The Dreki huts and campsite at the mouth of the Drekagil gorge. The path climbs west into the Dyngjufjöll.

points.name: Víti crater
points.note: An explosion crater with an opaque blue-green lake, on the rim above Öskjuvatn.

points.name: Öskjuvatn
points.note: The view over Öskjuvatn inside the caldera walls. Then 2.5 km north on the marked path to the Vikraborgir car park.
